name: WA-10
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+9 district with incumbent Marilyn Strickland running for re-election
Strickland has raised $1.9M with outside support; Chris Chung shows no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price a Democratic win around 96%
No public polls or expert ratings, so the outlook rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: Strickland combines a Democratic-leaning seat, a large fundraising advantage, and outside-group backing against a challenger with no visible financial footprint, while markets price the race as near-certain for Democrats. Every available signal points the same direction, keeping this firmly in Safe D territory.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending for Chung or unusually weak Strickland showing in the top-two primary results would be the first sign the margin could narrow.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Washington's 10th District leans Democratic by about nine points, and incumbent Marilyn Strickland is seeking another term. She has raised nearly $1.9 million and holds roughly $609,000 on hand, with outside groups adding support and none opposing her. Republican Chris Chung has no reported fundraising, leaving him with little visible campaign infrastructure heading into November.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which price Strickland's chances around 96 percent. A favorable seat, a well-funded incumbent, and a lightly financed challenger point to a comfortable Democratic win, though the absence of polling leaves some uncertainty about the exact margin.
